claims.claim: The binding affinities of PRC2CXC>A or PRC2EED>A were two- to three-fold lower than that of wild-type PRC2.

claims.claim: The binding affinity of PRC2CXC>A/EED>A was about five-fold lower compared to the wild-type complex.
claims.source: The binding affinities of PRC2CXC>A or PRC2EED>A were two- to three-fold lower than that of wild-type PRC2 and that of PRC2CXC>A/EED>A was about five-fold lower compared to the wild-type complex (Figure 2A,B, compare lanes 11–40 with 1–10).
claims.evidence: This is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 2A,B.

claims.claim: The PRC2CXC>A/EED>A complex still binds to nucleosomes with sub-micromolar affinity.
claims.source: The PRC2CXC>A/EED>A complex therefore still binds to nucleosomes with sub-micromolar affinity (Figure 2A, lanes 21–30).
claims.evidence: This is supported by EMSA data shown in Figure 2A.

claims.claim: PRC2CXC>A showed almost no detectable histone methyltransferase activity on mononucleosomes compared to wild-type PRC2.
claims.source: On the same mononucleosomes used above, PRC2CXC>A showed almost no detectable histone methyltransferase (HMTase) activity compared to wild-type PRC2 (Figure 2C, compare lanes 5–7 with 2–4, see also Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: On dinucleosomes, the PRC2CXC>A complex generates H3K27me1 and -me3 although much less efficiently than wild-type PRC2.
claims.source: Indeed, on dinucleosomes, the PRC2CXC>A complex does generate H3K27me1 and -me3 although still much less efficiently than wild-type PRC2 (Figure 2C, compare lanes 12–14 with 9–11).
claims.evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: PRC2CXC>A did not show reduced K27 methylation activity compared to wild-type PRC2 on H3 peptide substrate.
claims.source: However, it is important to note that PRC2CXC>A did not show reduced K27 methylation activity compared to wild-type PRC2 on this H3 peptide substrate (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This is supported by mass spectrometry-based HMTase assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: The mutations in the EZH2CXC domain do not appear to alter the conformation of EZH2 in a way that would directly interfere with catalysis.
claims.source: The mutations in the EZH2CXC domain therefore do not appear to alter the conformation of EZH2 in a way that would directly interfere with catalysis.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the peptide HMTase assay data.

claims.claim: Interaction of the EZH2CXC domain with the DNA on the substrate nucleosomes is a critical step for engaging the H3 N-terminus in a manner that allows effective H3K27 methylation.

claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the mutational and biochemical data.

claims.claim: The affinity of PRC2 for binding to mononucleosomes containing H3Kc36me3 was indistinguishable from that for binding to unmodified mononucleosomes.
claims.source: In EMSAs, the affinity of PRC2 for binding to mononucleosomes containing a trimethyllysine analog at H3K36 (H3Kc36me3) (Simon et al., 2007) was indistinguishable from that for binding to unmodified mononucleosomes (Figure 3A,B).

claims.source: As previously reported (Schmitges et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2011), on H3Kc36me3-containing mononucleosomes, H3K27 mono- and trimethylation by PRC2 was more than 10-fold inhibited (Figure 3C, compare lanes 5–7 with 2–4, see also Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).

claims.claim: Methylation of H3K27 was inhibited on mononucleosomes where H3K36 had been mutated to arginine (H3K36R).
claims.source: Methylation of H3K27 was also inhibited on mononucleosomes where H3K36 had been mutated to arginine (H3K36R) and, intriguingly, also on H3K36A mononucleosomes (Figure 3C, compare lanes 8–13 with 2–4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: Methylation of H3K27 was inhibited on H3K36A mononucleosomes.
claims.source: Methylation of H3K27 was also inhibited on mononucleosomes where H3K36 had been mutated to arginine (H3K36R) and, intriguingly, also on H3K36A mononucleosomes (Figure 3C, compare lanes 8–13 with 2–4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by HMTase assay data shown in Figure 3C.

claims.claim: PRC2 inhibition on H3K36R and H3K36A mononucleosomes was less severe than on H3Kc36me3 mononucleosomes.
claims.source: PRC2 inhibition on H3K36R and H3K36A mononucleosomes was less severe than on H3Kc36me3 mononucleosomes (Figure 3C, compare lanes 8–13 with 5–7).

claims.claim: The allosteric inhibition of PRC2 by H3K36me3 only occurs in the context of the geometric constraints of the nucleosome.
claims.source: The allosteric inhibition of PRC2 by H3K36me3 therefore only occurs in the context of the geometric constraints of the nucleosome.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparison of nucleosome and peptide HMTase assays.

claims.claim: DNA-binding by the winged-helix domain of PHF1 increases the binding affinity and residence time of PHF1-PRC2 on nucleosomes about two- to three-fold.

claims.claim: H3K27 mono- and tri-methylation by PHF1-PRC2 was strongly inhibited on H3Kc36me3 mononucleosomes.

claims.source: Specifically, 81% of H3K36R mutant animals arrested development at variable time points during larval growth, 18% developed to the end of third larval instar and formed pupae that died prior to metamorphosis, and 1% developed into late pupae that complete metamorphosis but then arrested as pharate adults (Figure 4).

claims.claim: 18% of H3K36R mutant animals developed to the end of third larval instar and formed pupae that died prior to metamorphosis.
claims.source: Specifically, 81% of H3K36R mutant animals arrested development at variable time points during larval growth, 18% developed to the end of third larval instar and formed pupae that died prior to metamorphosis, and 1% developed into late pupae that complete metamorphosis but then arrested as pharate adults (Figure 4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by developmental analysis shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: 1% of H3K36R mutant animals developed into late pupae that complete metamorphosis but then arrested as pharate adults.
claims.source: Specifically, 81% of H3K36R mutant animals arrested development at variable time points during larval growth, 18% developed to the end of third larval instar and formed pupae that died prior to metamorphosis, and 1% developed into late pupae that complete metamorphosis but then arrested as pharate adults (Figure 4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by developmental analysis shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: H3K36R mutant pharate adults consistently showed homeotic transformations reminiscent of polycomb group mutants.
claims.source: When we dissected the rare H3K36R mutant pharate adults from their pupal cases and examined their epidermal structures, we found that they consistently showed homeotic transformations reminiscent of polycomb group (PcG) mutants.
claims.evidence: This is supported by phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: PcG mutant phenotypes in H3K36R mutants included antenna-to-leg transformations and extra sex comb teeth on meso- and meta-thoracic legs in males.
claims.source: These PcG mutant phenotypes included antenna-to-leg transformations and extra sex comb teeth on meso- and meta-thoracic legs in males (Figure 4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by phenotypic analysis shown in Figure 4.

claims.claim: 96% of H3K36A mutant animals arrested development before hatching from the eggshell.

claims.claim: H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 bulk levels were reduced more than 4-fold in H3K36R mutant larvae compared to wildtype.

claims.claim: In H3K36A mutants, H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 bulk levels were reduced about 3- to 4-fold compared to wildtype.
claims.source: In H3K36A mutants, H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 bulk levels were reduced about 3- to 4-fold compared to wildtype (Figure 5B, compare lanes 5–8 with 1–4).
claims.evidence: This is supported by western blot data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: In both H3K36A and H3K36R mutant embryos, H3K27me3 bulk levels appeared largely unchanged compared to wildtype.
claims.source: In both genotypes, H3K27me3 bulk levels appeared largely unchanged compared to wildtype (Figure 5B, compare lanes 5–8 and 9–12 with 1–4).

claims.source: Both mutants showed stochastic misexpression of Abd-B in single cells or pairs of cells in the CNS of late-stage embryos (Figure 6A).

claims.evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: The stochastic misexpression of multiple HOX genes in animals with chromatin consisting of H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes is caused by defective Polycomb repression as a result of the reduced H3K27me3 levels in HOX gene chromatin.
claims.source: The most straightforward explanation for the stochastic misexpression of multiple HOX genes in animals with chromatin consisting of H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes therefore is that it is caused by defective Polycomb repression as a result of the reduced H3K27me3 levels in HOX gene chromatin.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the combined genetic and molecular data.

claims.claim: Different forms of PRC2 use the same molecular interactions for binding the H3 N-terminus on substrate nucleosomes.
claims.source: Consistent with our findings here, an independent recent study of a cryo-EM structure of PRC2 with co-factors JARID2 and AEBP2 bound to a mononucleosome with monoubiquitylated H2A (Kasinath et al., 2020) identified very similar interactions of EZH2 with the nucleosomal DNA and the H3 N-terminus.
claims.evidence: This is supported by comparison with an independent study.

claims.claim: Unmodified H3K36 has the right fit for interaction of the H3 N-terminus with the EZH2 surface and placement of H3K27 in the active site.
claims.source: Unmodified H3K36 has the right fit for interaction of the H3 N-terminus with the EZH2 surface and placement of H3K27 in the active site.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the structural and biochemical data.

claims.claim: H3K36me2/3, H3K36R or H3K36A alterations of the side chain of residue 36 in H3 impair productive interaction of H3K27 with the catalytic center of EZH2.
claims.source: The inhibition of H3K27 mono-, di- and tri-methylation on nucleosomes carrying H3K36me2 or -me3 (Schmitges et al., 2011; Yuan et al., 2011) or on H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes (Figure 3C) suggests that even though these side chains could theoretically be accommodated in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface, these alterations of the side chain of residue 36 in H3 chain must somehow impair productive interaction of H3K27 with the catalytic center of EZH2.
claims.evidence: This is an inference based on the biochemical data.

claims.claim: Docking of the H3K36 side chain in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface is critical for rapid alignment of the H3 N-terminus on the EZH2 surface into a catalytically competent state.
claims.source: Taken together, a possible scenario would therefore be that within the time frame of the PRC2-nucleosome binding and reaction cycle, docking of the H3K36 side chain in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface is critical for rapid alignment of the H3 N-terminus on the EZH2 surface into a catalytically competent state.
claims.evidence: This is a speculative model proposed to explain the data.

claims.claim: H3K36me2/3 does not locally disrupt nucleosome binding but allosterically inhibits H3K27 from interacting with the EZH2 active site.
claims.source: According to this view, H3K36me2/3 does not locally disrupt nucleosome binding but allosterically inhibits H3K27 from interacting with the EZH2 active site.
claims.evidence: This is a mechanistic interpretation of the data.

claims.claim: PRC2 is unable to effectively deposit high levels of H3K27me3 on the H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes in Drosophila chromatin.
claims.source: A simple straightforward explanation for these phenotypes in H3K36R or H3K36A mutant animals is that PRC2 is unable to effectively deposit high levels of H3K27me3 on the H3K36R or H3K36A nucleosomes, respectively, in their chromatin.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the in vivo genetic and molecular data.

claims.claim: H3K27me3 levels at HOX genes are below the threshold needed to stringently maintain Polycomb repression in H3K36R or H3K36A mutants, causing stochastic misexpression.
claims.source: Accordingly, H3K27me3 levels at HOX genes are below the threshold needed to stringently maintain Polycomb repression and consequently, HOX genes become stochastically misexpressed in a fraction of cells.
claims.evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic and molecular data.

claims.claim: It is the exquisite geometry formed by a relay of interactions between the PRC2 enzyme, nucleosomal DNA and the H3 N-terminus that enable H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 to allosterically prevent PRC2 from depositing H3K27me3 at transcribed genes.
claims.source: The structural, biochemical and genetic work reported in this study shows that it is the exquisite geometry formed by a relay of interactions between the PRC2 enzyme, nucleosomal DNA and the H3 N-terminus that enable the histone methylation marks H3K36me2 and H3K36me3 in transcriptionally active chromatin to allosterically prevent PRC2 from depositing the repressive histone methylation mark H3K27me3 at transcribed genes.
claims.evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, integrating all the data.

results.result: The cryo-EM structure of PHF1-PRC2 bound to dinucleosomes at 5.2 Å overall resolution (4.4 Å focused) reveals how EZH2 binding to nucleosomal DNA orients the H3 N-terminus (residues R26-K37) through an extended network of interactions to position H3K27 in the active site. Unmodified H3K36 occupies a critical position in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface, with its epsilon-amino group engaging Q570 and possibly the DNA phosphate backbone.
results.evaluation: Claims C3, C17-C32 collectively describe the cryo-EM structure determination and modeling of the PRC2-dinucleosome complex. The resolution values (5.2 Å overall, 4.4 Å focused) are directly stated with supporting data processing workflows (Figure 1 supplements). The structural model of H3 residues R26-K37 is supported by well-defined density (C21, Figure 1F). The positioning of H3K36 in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface is supported by structural data (C28-C29, Figure 1F and supplements). The comparison with the previously proposed E579 pocket (C31-C32) provides critical context showing incompatibility with the current structure.

results.result: Mutations in the EZH2CXC domain (K563A Q565A K569A Q570A) reduce PRC2 nucleosome binding affinity 2-3 fold and nearly abolish H3K27 methylation activity on mononucleosomes, while activity is partially restored on dinucleosomes. The mutations do not affect catalytic activity on free H3 peptides, indicating that EZH2CXC-DNA interaction is critical for engaging the H3 N-terminus on nucleosomes for effective H3K27 methylation.
results.evaluation: Claims C33-C41 describe systematic mutational analysis of the EZH2CXC domain. EMSA data (C33-C36, Figure 2A-B) quantitatively demonstrate modest effects on binding affinity. HMTase assays (C37-C38, Figure 2C) show dramatic loss of activity on mononucleosomes but partial restoration on dinucleosomes. The peptide control experiment (C39, Figure 2 supplement 1B) is critical for ruling out direct catalytic defects. The conclusion (C41) logically follows from the combined data showing that DNA binding by EZH2CXC is required for productive substrate engagement.

results.result: H3K36me3, H3K36R, and H3K36A modifications all inhibit H3K27 methylation by PRC2 on nucleosomes in vitro (>10-fold for H3K36me3, less severe for H3K36R/A) without affecting nucleosome binding affinity. Importantly, H3K36me3 does not inhibit H3K27 methylation on free H3 peptides, demonstrating that allosteric inhibition requires the geometric constraints of the nucleosome.
results.evaluation: Claims C4-C5, C42-C48 describe comprehensive biochemical characterization of H3K36 variants. EMSA data (C42, Figure 3A-B) show no binding defect for H3K36me3. HMTase assays (C43-C46, Figure 3C) quantitatively demonstrate inhibition by H3K36me3, H3K36R, and H3K36A on nucleosomes. The critical peptide control (C47, Figure 3D) shows no inhibition on free peptides, strongly supporting the allosteric mechanism conclusion (C48). The data are internally consistent and support the model that unmodified H3K36 provides optimal fit in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface.

results.result: Full-length PHF1-PRC2, which has higher nucleosome binding affinity and residence time than core PRC2, is still strongly inhibited by H3K36me3 on mononucleosomes.
results.evaluation: Claims C50-C51 extend the inhibition mechanism to PHF1-PRC2. HMTase data (C50, Figure 3 supplement 1C) demonstrate strong inhibition despite enhanced binding properties. This result is important for showing that increased binding affinity/residence time cannot overcome the allosteric inhibition mechanism, supporting the geometric model proposed from the structure.

results.result: Drosophila H3K36R mutants complete embryogenesis with normal cuticle morphology but show variable developmental arrest: 81% during larval stages, 18% as pupae, and 1% as pharate adults displaying Polycomb-like homeotic transformations (antenna-to-leg, extra sex combs). H3K36A mutants show more severe phenotypes with 96% arresting before hatching.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C59 describe detailed developmental phenotyping of H3K36 mutants. The quantitative developmental staging data (C52-C55, Figure 4) are clearly presented with sample sizes. The homeotic transformation phenotypes (C56-C57, Figure 4) are characteristic of Polycomb mutants and well-documented. The difference between H3K36R strains (C53 vs C58) is noted and discussed in Methods. The H3K36A phenotype (C59) is consistent with the in vitro data showing inhibition. The phenotypic data provide strong in vivo validation of the biochemical findings.

results.result: H3K36R mutant larvae show >4-fold reduction in H3K36me2/me3 bulk levels and ~2-fold reduction in H3K27me3, with 3-4 fold reduction specifically at HOX genes (Ubx, abd-A, Abd-B, Antp). In H3K36A and H3K36R mutant embryos, H3K27me3 bulk levels appear unchanged but are ~1.5-fold reduced at HOX loci.
results.evaluation: Claims C60-C68 describe comprehensive molecular characterization by western blot and ChIP-seq. Western blot data (C60-C63, Figure 5A-B) quantitatively show histone modification changes with appropriate loading controls. ChIP-seq data (C64-C68, Figure 5C-F) provide genome-wide validation with proper normalization using spike-in controls. The differential effects at HOX genes versus genome-wide are clearly demonstrated. The apparent discrepancy between embryos and larvae (C63 vs C61) is appropriately noted and likely reflects incomplete H3 replacement in embryos as discussed in the text.

results.result: H3K36R and H3K36A mutants show stochastic misexpression of multiple HOX genes (Abd-B, Ubx, Antp) in specific tissues (CNS, imaginal discs) where these genes are normally repressed by Polycomb. The misexpression is less widespread than in strong PcG mutants (H3K27R, esc-) and correlates with reduced H3K27me3 levels at HOX genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C69-C75 describe detailed HOX gene expression analysis by immunohistochemistry/immunofluorescence. The stochastic misexpression patterns (C69, C71-C74, Figure 6) are well-documented with quantitative penetrance data (50% for Ubx in wing discs, 100% for Antp in antenna). The comparison with strong PcG mutants (C70, Figure 6A) provides important context. The conclusion (C75) that misexpression results from reduced H3K27me3 is well-supported by the correlation between molecular (Figure 5) and phenotypic (Figure 6) data. The tissue-specific patterns are consistent with known PcG biology.

results.result: The structural, biochemical, and genetic data collectively support a model where the geometry formed by interactions between PRC2, nucleosomal DNA, and the H3 N-terminus enables allosteric inhibition by H3K36me2/3. Unmodified H3K36 provides optimal fit for productive H3K27 methylation, while methylated or mutated H3K36 impairs catalytic competence without disrupting binding, preventing effective H3K27me3 deposition at transcriptionally active genes.
results.evaluation: Claims C76-C83 represent the integrated conclusions of the study. The model is well-supported by convergent evidence: (1) structural data showing H3K36 position in the EZH2CXC-DNA interface (C3-C4, C28-C29), (2) biochemical data showing inhibition by H3K36 modifications on nucleosomes but not peptides (C43-C48), (3) mutational data showing EZH2CXC-DNA interaction is critical (C37-C41), and (4) in vivo data showing reduced H3K27me3 and HOX misexpression in H3K36R/A mutants (C60-C75). The allosteric mechanism (C78-C80) is supported by the lack of binding defects (C42) and peptide activity (C47). The model is internally consistent and explains all major observations.

results.result: Background claims establishing that PRC2 trimethylates H3K27, H3K27me3 recruits PRC1 and activates PRC2 in trans, while H3K4me3 and H3K36me2/3 inhibit PRC2 in cis by reducing kcat without major effects on binding affinity.
results.evaluation: Claims C1, C9-C16 represent well-established background knowledge supported by extensive prior literature (multiple citations provided). These claims provide essential context for the current study but are not novel findings. The citations appear appropriate and the statements are consistent with the field's understanding of PRC2 regulation.

results.result: Di- and tri-methylated H3K36 inhibit PRC2 at transcriptionally active genes.
results.evaluation: Claim C2 is supported both by prior literature (citations provided) and by the new data in this manuscript (Figures 3, 5). This represents a key biological context for the study, bridging prior knowledge with the new mechanistic insights.

results.result: DNA-binding by the PHF1 winged-helix domain increases PHF1-PRC2 binding affinity and residence time on nucleosomes 2-3 fold, resulting in more efficient H3K27 methylation.
results.evaluation: Claim C49 is supported by citation to prior work (Choi et al., 2017) and provides context for the PHF1-PRC2 experiments in this study. This is established prior knowledge used to interpret the current findings.
